operations.description:
Create a new employment contract for an employee.

This operation adds a new contract record to the employee's historical employment record within the current organization context. A contract captures the employee's start date, optional end date, compensation terms, weekly working-hour expectation, and optional notes. The employee is identified by the path parameter, and the new contract is always created in the scope of that employee.

When a new contract is created, the system must close the previous active contract for the same employee by setting its end date to the day before the new contract starts. This preserves a continuous employment history and ensures that only one active contract exists at a time. Past contracts remain immutable historical records after they are no longer active.

Access is restricted to users who are allowed to manage employee data or view contract records according to organization permissions. The system must reject attempts to create overlapping active contracts, invalid pay periods, or contract data that does not satisfy the required dates and compensation terms. Because contracts belong to employees, all reads and writes must remain isolated to the current organization.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target employee by employeeId within the current organization context and verify the caller has employee management access for contract creation. Reject the request if the employee does not exist, belongs to another organization, or is inaccessible in the current tenant scope.

Validate the payload using the actual contract fields only: startDate, endDate, payRate, payPeriod, workingHoursPerWeek, and notes. Enforce that startDate and payRate are present, payPeriod is one of hourly/daily/weekly/monthly, and workingHoursPerWeek is provided. Reject invalid date ordering where endDate exists and is before startDate. Because the schema exposes deleted_at but business rules treat contracts as historical records, do not expose any manual delete behavior here.

Before inserting the new row, find the current active contract for the same employee using the existing date-range rules and close it by setting its endDate to the day before the new startDate. Perform this in a transaction so the update of the previous active contract and insertion of the new contract are atomic. If a contract with the same employee and startDate already exists, return a validation conflict based on the unique constraint.

Persist the new contract row with the employee foreign key from the path and audit timestamps. Return the created contract entity. If business rules or persistence checks fail, surface a clear domain validation error rather than partially updating the employee's history.

responseBody.description: The newly created employee contract record, including its persisted dates, compensation terms, and timestamps.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single employee contract record for viewing contract history.

This operation returns one historical employment contract belonging to a specific employee within the current organization context. The contract contains the employee’s effective date range, compensation terms, working-time expectations, and optional notes, allowing consumers to review how the employee’s employment arrangement was defined at that point in time.

The contract is part of an employee’s immutable history. Consumers can use this endpoint to inspect the active or past contract details for the employee, while authorization rules ensure that employees may view their own contracts and users with employee view permission may view any employee’s contracts in the organization. The employee relationship is organization-scoped, so the request must be validated against both the employee and contract identifiers before returning data.

If the employee does not exist in the current organization, the contract does not belong to that employee, or the caller lacks permission to view the record, the request must be rejected with the appropriate not-found or authorization error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the employee record by employeeId within the current organization context, then load the contract by contractId constrained to that employeeId. Do not allow cross-employee access: the contract must belong to the same employee referenced in the path. Because both ids are UUID primary keys, validate them as UUID path parameters.

Return the full contract entity with all persisted fields: id, employee reference, start date, end date, pay rate, pay period, working hours per week, notes, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at if present in the persisted record. Do not fabricate any derived fields.

Enforce authorization using the organization-scoped employee view rule: the caller may read their own contract history, or must have employee:view permission to read another employee’s contracts. Reject requests outside the current organization context. If the employee-contract relation is missing, return not found rather than exposing whether the contract exists globally. Because this is a historical record, no mutation logic is involved.

operations.description:
Update the current active contract for an employee.

This operation lets authorized users change the active employment terms for a specific employee within the currently selected organization. The contract record is part of the employee’s historical employment record, so the API must preserve past contracts and only allow editing when the target contract is still the active one.

The contract stores the employee reference, effective dates, compensation terms, pay period, weekly working hours, and optional notes. When the updated contract affects the active period, the service must validate the date range, ensure the employee belongs to the current organization, and reject attempts to modify past contracts. If the caller does not have employee-view access for the target employee, the request must be denied.

If the update changes the contract start date while preserving it as the active contract, the implementation must ensure the employee still has at most one active contract and must prevent overlaps with other contracts. Validation errors should be returned for invalid dates, unsupported pay periods, missing required contract fields, or attempts to edit an immutable historical contract.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the target employee and contract within the current organization context using both path identifiers. Verify the employee exists, belongs to the selected organization, and the contract belongs to that employee. Enforce authorization: the caller may update their own active contract only if permitted by the business rules, while updating another employee’s contract requires employee manage permission; if access is only through viewing, reject with a permission error.

Confirm the contract is the active contract before applying changes. Past contracts must not be modified. Validate all incoming fields against the schema and business rules: start date is required, pay rate is required, pay period must be one of hourly/daily/weekly/monthly, working hours per week are required, notes are optional, and end date may be null. Reject updates that would create overlapping active periods or violate the one-active-contract rule.

Use a transaction when persisting updates so the employee’s contract history remains consistent. If the contract start date or end date changes, re-evaluate whether the contract remains active and whether surrounding contract dates still form a continuous history. Do not auto-edit older contracts unless required by a direct contract-rollover workflow; this endpoint should only update the addressed contract.

Return the updated contract entity after persistence. If the contract cannot be found, return a not-found error. If the contract is not active, return a validation or conflict error indicating the record is immutable. If organization context is missing or mismatched, reject the request as unauthorized or forbidden.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of departments for the currently selected organization.

This endpoint is used to browse the organization’s internal department structure, including parent-child relationships and department descriptions. Employees can use it to understand how the organization is grouped, while users with management permission can use the same list to locate departments for editing or deletion.

The result is restricted to the active organization context. Departments from other organizations must never be returned. The list should honor the current hierarchy and exclude records that are not visible according to the organization’s department browsing rules. Search, filtering, pagination, and sorting should be supported for department name, parent department, and deletion state where applicable.

If the organization context is missing or invalid, or if the caller attempts to browse outside the selected organization, the request must be rejected. The operation must respect the unique department naming rule within an organization and avoid exposing duplicate or cross-tenant department data.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_time_departments using the selected organization context from the authentication/session layer.
Apply a mandatory filter on erp_hrm_time_organization_id to enforce tenant isolation.
Support pagination, free-text search on name, and optional filtering by parent department and deleted state if the request DTO includes those controls. Sort results deterministically, preferably by name and then created_at for stable paging.

Return summary rows only, not full relationship graphs, to keep the list lightweight. Include parent department identifiers or summary references only if the summary schema supports them. Do not join across organizations. If the search term matches no rows, return an empty page rather than an error.

Because the schema defines @@unique([erp_hrm_time_organization_id, name]), treat department names as organization-scoped. Do not attempt to infer or expose duplicate structures across tenants. Use the existing deleted_at column only for filtering if the list is meant to show archived/removed departments; otherwise, return active records according to the business browsing rule. If the caller lacks access to the selected organization, reject the request as unauthorized/forbidden.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of department summaries for the selected organization.

operations.description:
Create a department for the currently selected organization.

Departments are organizational groupings used to organize employees and describe the organization’s internal structure. This operation lets organization managers add a new department with a name, an optional description, and an optional parent department so the organization can represent a simple one-level hierarchy.

The department belongs only to the active organization context. The parent department, if provided, must also belong to the same organization and must not create a deeper hierarchy. If the request would create a duplicate or unclear department structure, the request is rejected. Employees can view departments through read operations, but only users with organization management permission can create them.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Insert a new record into erp_hrm_time_departments using the currently selected organization context as the owning scope.

Validate that the caller has organization management permission. Require a department name. Accept an optional description and optional parent department reference. If a parent is supplied, verify that it exists, belongs to the same organization, and does not violate the single-level hierarchy rule.

Before inserting, check for duplicate or conflicting department structures within the same organization, including cases where the same name/parent combination would create an ambiguous structure. Reject the request if the target organization context is missing or if the parent belongs to another organization.

Return the created department after persistence. If the underlying schema uses an organization foreign key or parent foreign key, populate them from context and validated input only. Do not modify employees here; employee department clearing is handled by delete operations elsewhere.

requestBody.description: Department details to create within the current organization.

operations.description:
Retrieve the full details of a department within the currently selected organization.

Departments are organization-scoped records used to organize employees and describe the internal structure of the organization. This endpoint returns the department identity, name, optional description, optional parent department reference, and audit timestamps so callers can display or inspect the department in context.

The returned department must belong to the active organization context. If the department does not exist in the selected organization, the request must be rejected. The response is intended for both management screens and read-only employee views that need to show the organizational structure.

If the department has a parent department, the relationship should be preserved in the returned representation. Any organization mismatch, missing department, or inaccessible record should produce an appropriate not-found or forbidden error from the service layer.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the department by UUID primary key and ensure it belongs to the currently selected organization. Use a query constrained by department id and organization id to prevent cross-organization access.

Return the complete department record when found. Include name, description, parent_department_id, created_at, and updated_at as defined by the schema. Do not expose deleted records as valid detail results if the repository filters them out by lifecycle policy.

If the department does not exist in the selected organization, return a not-found error. If the caller lacks access to the current organization context, return a forbidden or unauthorized error according to the auth middleware contract. Because this is a detail endpoint, do not perform any write-side cascade or employee reassignment logic.

operations.description:
Update a department within the selected organization.

Departments are organization-scoped structural labels used to organize employees and reflect the internal hierarchy of the organization. This operation lets authorized users change the department name, description, and parent department while preserving the department's identity and organization ownership.

The department hierarchy is limited to one level of nesting. The parent department, when provided, must belong to the same organization and must not create deeper nesting or a duplicate/confusing structure. Department names must remain unique within the organization.

If a department is removed elsewhere in the system, employees assigned to it are cleared from that department rather than being deleted. This update operation must reject requests that target a department outside the currently selected organization or that would violate department uniqueness or hierarchy rules.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the target department by id and verify it belongs to the currently selected organization. Reject the request if the department does not exist, is deleted, or is outside the selected organization context.

Validate mutable fields from IErpHrmTimeDepartment.IUpdate: name, description, and parentDepartmentId (or equivalent parent reference defined by the DTO). Enforce organization-scoped uniqueness of department name using the existing unique constraint on (organization_id, name). Reject updates that would create duplicate or confusing department structures within the same organization.

When a parent department is supplied, verify the parent belongs to the same organization, is not the same department, and does not introduce nesting deeper than one level. Since the schema is self-referential, prevent cycles and multi-level chains by ensuring the chosen parent has no parent of its own if the business rule requires a strict one-level tree.

Persist the update in a transaction. Do not modify employees directly during this operation. Employee department clearing happens only when a department is deleted, not on ordinary update. Return the updated department entity after save.

responseBody.description: Updated department record in the selected organization.

parameters.description: Department identifier within the selected organization (UUID).
parameters.name: departmentId

requestBody.description: Fields used to update a department's name, description, and parent department.

operations.description:
Permanently removes a department from the selected organization.

This operation is used to maintain the organization’s internal structure when a team or reporting line is no longer needed. When a department is deleted, any employees assigned to that department keep their employee records, but their department assignment is cleared so that historical employee data remains intact.

The deletion is limited to the current organization context and does not affect departments in other organizations. Clients should expect permission checks and validation failures when the department does not exist, is outside the current organization, or the caller lacks organization management permission.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the department within the current organization context by departmentId and verify the caller has organization management permission. If the department is not found in the selected organization, return a not-found error.

Before deleting the department row, query employees referencing this department and update those employee records so their department reference becomes null. Preserve all employee records and do not cascade-delete employees.

Delete the department record in the same transaction after clearing employee assignments. Ensure the operation respects the one-level department hierarchy: deleting a parent department removes that department only, while the employees linked to it are disassociated. Return an error if the caller lacks access or if the department cannot be deleted due to domain constraints enforced by persistence rules.

parameters.description: The department identifier within the selected organization.
parameters.name: departmentId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of roles for the currently selected organization.

This operation returns both built-in and custom roles that belong to the active organization context. Roles are organization-specific, so the result is always scoped to the user’s selected organization and never crosses tenant boundaries. The list is intended for role management screens where owners and other authorized members need to browse role names, descriptions, built-in status, and related permission sets.

The response is optimized for pagination and search. Consumers can filter roles by built-in status and search by role name or description to find the relevant role quickly. Built-in roles such as Owner, Manager, and Employee remain part of the organization’s baseline access model and are included in the list, while custom roles reflect organization-defined access responsibility.

If the organization context is missing or the caller lacks permission to view roles, the request must be rejected. The service must also ensure that only roles belonging to the active organization are returned, and it should not expose permission catalog records directly except through the role’s assigned permission summary.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the active organization from the authenticated member context and query erp_hrm_time_roles by erp_hrm_time_organization_id. Support pagination, sorting, and search terms in the request body. Search should match role name and optional description. Allow filtering by built-in status and, if supported by the DTO, by assigned permission keys through joins to erp_hrm_time_role_permissions and erp_hrm_time_permissions.

Always exclude roles from other organizations. Use a count query for pagination metadata and return role summaries only, not the full normalized permission join rows. Preserve stable ordering when multiple sort keys are provided. If the organization context is absent, return a context/authorization error. If the caller lacks role-view access according to the organization permission model, deny the request.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of role summaries for the selected organization.

requestBody.description: Search, pagination, and sorting criteria for organization roles.

operations.description:
Create a new role within the currently selected organization.

This operation creates an organization-scoped role record for the active tenant context. The caller must have the appropriate role-management permission in the selected organization, and the role name must be unique within that organization.

If the request includes approved permissions, the system stores the role and its permission assignments together so the resulting role can be used immediately for membership-based access control in that organization. Validation errors are returned when the organization context is missing, the caller is not allowed to manage roles, the role name already exists, or any requested permission is not part of the approved permission catalog.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Insert a new record into erp_hrm_time_roles using the current organization context and validate that the caller has organization owner or equivalent role-management permission. Enforce uniqueness of (erp_hrm_time_organization_id, name) before insert. Reject attempts to create built-in roles through this endpoint unless the business layer explicitly permits system-seeded bootstrap data; normal API usage should create custom roles only.

If permissions are included in the request, validate every requested permission against erp_hrm_time_permissions by key or identifier, then create erp_hrm_time_role_permissions rows for each approved permission in the same transaction as the role insert. Roll back the entire transaction if any permission is invalid or any insert fails.

Return the created role entity after persistence. Ensure the response reflects the organization-scoped role record and, if the component schema includes nested permissions, populate them from the join table. Do not allow cross-organization role creation, and do not accept any organization identifier from the request body if the current organization context already determines scope.

responseBody.description: The newly created organization-scoped role record, including its assigned permissions when available.

requestBody.description: Role creation data for the currently selected organization.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single organization role in the current organization context.

This operation returns the role record associated with the active tenant, so consumers can inspect role details before assignment or editing. Roles are organization-scoped, and access to the returned data is evaluated against the selected organization membership.

If the role is not found in the current organization context, the server must return a not-found error. If the caller does not have permission to view role data, the request must be rejected according to the organization access rules.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the role by `id` within the current organization context and ensure the row belongs to the active organization. Use a single indexed lookup by primary key, then verify `erp_hrm_time_organization_id` matches the request context to prevent cross-tenant access.

Return the complete role entity. Do not expose any derived permission assignment data from this endpoint unless the base role representation already includes it in the shared component schema. The `is_builtin` flag must be preserved so downstream consumers can distinguish protected baseline roles from editable custom roles.

Handle not-found and unauthorized cases explicitly. If the role exists but belongs to a different organization, respond as not found to avoid tenant leakage. No mutation or side effects occur in this operation.

responseBody.description: The full role record for the current organization context.

parameters.description: Role identifier in the current organization context (UUID).
parameters.name: roleId

operations.description:
Update a role within the current organization.

This operation edits an organization-scoped role definition, including the role name and its assigned permission set when the role is a custom role. It is intended for organization owners and other authorized users managing access responsibility inside the selected tenant.

Built-in roles such as Owner, Manager, and Employee are part of the organization’s fixed access model and must remain unchanged. The service must verify that the target role belongs to the current organization, enforce role-edit permissions, and reject requests that attempt to modify immutable built-in roles or permissions outside the approved catalog.

If validation fails, the API should return a clear error for missing or invalid role data, a forbidden response for insufficient permission, and a not-found response when the role does not belong to the active organization.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the target role by roleId within the current organization context. Verify that the authenticated member has permission to update roles in this organization, and ensure the role is not one of the built-in Owner, Manager, or Employee roles when the business rule disallows modification.

Validate the request body according to IErpHrmTimeRole.IUpdate. Apply changes only to mutable fields supported by the schema. If the role includes a permission relation, replace or reconcile the assigned permission set according to the submitted payload while ensuring every permission exists in erp_hrm_time_permissions and belongs to the approved catalog.

Prevent cross-organization updates by scoping the lookup to the selected organization. Return 404 if the role is missing in the active tenant. Return 409 or 422 if the update would violate role rules, such as attempting to edit an immutable built-in role or assigning unsupported permissions. Persist the changes atomically and return the updated role entity.

responseBody.description: The updated role after the changes have been applied.

parameters.description: The role identifier within the current organization.
parameters.name: roleId

requestBody.description: The role fields to update, including the role name and permission assignment changes for a custom role.

operations.description:
Permanently removes a role from the current organization when business rules allow it.

This operation is intended for organization owners who manage custom role structures and need to remove obsolete roles from the organization’s access model. The built-in Owner, Manager, and Employee roles remain available in every organization and cannot be removed.

Before deletion, the service must verify that the role belongs to the selected organization, is not a built-in role, and is not assigned to any employees. If the role is still in use, the request must be rejected so that every employee in the organization continues to hold exactly one valid role.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the role by roleId within the current organization context.
Reject the request with a not-found error if the role does not exist in the selected organization.
Reject the request with a conflict or validation error if the role is built-in (Owner, Manager, or Employee).
Reject the request with a conflict error if any employee in the organization is assigned to the role.
If the role is custom and unassigned, delete the role in a transaction. Ensure related role-permission assignments are removed consistently according to foreign key rules or explicit cascading logic.
Do not alter employee records except by preventing deletion when the role is still assigned.
Do not expose any cross-organization role data. All checks must be scoped to the authenticated member’s selected organization.
Return no body on success.

parameters.description: The role identifier within the current organization context.
parameters.name: roleId

operations.description:
Retrieve the approved organization permission catalog.

This endpoint returns the platform-defined permissions that can be assigned to custom roles within the currently selected organization. It is intended for role creation and role editing flows, where organization owners and other authorized members must choose from the approved permission list rather than inventing new access rights.

The returned permission records represent the fixed business abilities used across the ERP HRM and time tracking platform, including organization management, employee management and viewing, project management and viewing, time management, time approval, viewing all time records, and report viewing. These records are reference data and are not created or edited through this API.

Access to this endpoint follows the organization’s active context and the caller’s authorization rules. If the organization context is missing or the caller lacks permission to manage or inspect role configuration, the request should be rejected. Filtering, pagination, and sorting should be applied consistently so the permission catalog can be reused in UI role selectors and admin tools.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Read the approved permission catalog from erp_hrm_time_permissions.
Apply organization context checks even though the permission set is global/reference data, because the caller must still be authorized within the selected organization to use role-management UI flows.
Support pagination, search, and sorting in the request body to satisfy the index contract. Search should match permission code/name/description fields exposed by the schema. Sorting should allow stable ordering, defaulting to a deterministic field such as name or code if present in the schema; do not assume fields that do not exist.
Return only permissions from the approved list used for custom roles. Do not expose any mechanism to create, update, or delete permissions. If the organization context is absent, return a validation/authorization error. If the request references unsupported filters or sort fields, reject it as invalid input.
Use a service query that is lightweight and cache-friendly because permissions are static reference data. If the schema includes audit or status columns, preserve them in the response only if they are part of the permission definition; otherwise return summary fields only.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of approved permission records available for organization role configuration.

requestBody.description: Search, pagination, and sorting criteria for browsing the approved permission catalog.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single approved permission from the platform’s canonical permission catalog.

This operation returns the permission key and human-readable description for one permission record so role-management screens can inspect the exact access capability before assigning it to an organization role. The permission catalog is the source of truth for valid permission values used by custom roles and access control rules.

The permission record is identified by its UUID primary key. If the permission does not exist, the server must return a not-found error. Because this endpoint reads from the global approved permission catalog, it does not depend on organization context and does not accept a request body.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load a single row from erp_hrm_time_permissions by id using the UUID path parameter.
Return the permission only if it exists and is not deleted_at-marked inactive; otherwise return not found.
Do not join to other tables because the permission catalog is self-contained.
The endpoint is read-only and must not require organization context.
Keep the response stable for role-editing workflows by returning the canonical permission entity fields only.

responseBody.description: The approved permission record from the canonical permission catalog.

parameters.description: Permission identifier (global scope).
parameters.name: permissionId

operations.description:
Assign an approved permission to a role within the selected organization.

This operation adds one permission to the specified role and is intended for organization role administration. Roles are organization-scoped, and the permission being attached must come from the platform's approved permission catalog. Built-in roles and custom roles share the same assignment model, but the caller must still respect organization ownership and access-control rules.

The created association is stored through the role-permission relation, which links a role record to an approved permission record. Duplicate assignments are rejected, and permissions outside the approved list are not allowed. If the role does not belong to the current organization, or if the caller lacks permission to manage roles, the request must fail with an authorization or validation error.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Resolve the role by roleId and verify it belongs to the current organization context. Require permission-management authorization according to the selected organization's access rules, typically owner-level role administration.

Validate that the requested permission exists in the approved permission catalog and is not deleted. Reject the request if the permission key is not one of the approved organization permissions. Resolve the permission by key or identifier as defined by the create DTO, then insert a row into erp_hrm_time_role_permissions with the role id and permission id.

Prevent duplicates by checking the unique pair (erp_hrm_time_role_id, erp_hrm_time_permission_id). If the pair already exists, return a conflict-style validation failure. Use a transaction so concurrent requests cannot create duplicate role-permission rows. Return the newly created relation with its linked role and permission references if the API contract expects a full object.

responseBody.description: The created role-permission assignment.

parameters.description: Role identifier within the current organization.
parameters.name: roleId

requestBody.description: Permission assignment payload containing one approved permission to attach to the role.

operations.description:
Update the permission set assigned to a role within the currently selected organization.

This operation lets an organization owner or another authorized member with role-management capability change what a role can do. It applies to organization-scoped roles and enforces the approved permission catalog so that only valid business permissions can be attached to a role.

Built-in roles remain governed by the organization’s access model, while custom roles can be adjusted to match the organization’s current structure. The system validates the requested permissions, rejects any value outside the approved list, and preserves the role’s organization scope. If the role is currently assigned to employees, the update affects their access immediately within the selected organization.

If the role cannot be found in the active organization, the request fails with a not-found error. If the caller lacks authorization, the request fails with an access error. If the permission set contains invalid or unsupported entries, the request fails with a validation error.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the target role by roleId and ensure it belongs to the current organization context. Verify the caller is authorized to manage roles and permission assignments according to organization access rules.

Accept a request body containing the full desired permission set for the role. Validate each permission against the approved permission catalog; reject any permission outside the allowed list. Preserve the role identity, name, organization, and built-in/custom classification; only modify the permission assignment data.

If the role is built-in, enforce any schema or business constraints that prevent unsupported permission changes. If the role is custom, update the stored permission set atomically so that concurrent edits cannot partially apply. Return the updated role permissions after persistence.

Handle errors explicitly: return not found when the role does not exist in the current organization, forbidden when the caller cannot manage roles, and bad request when the permission set is missing, empty when not allowed, duplicated, or contains unsupported values. Record any required audit/activity entry if the service layer uses activity logging for role changes.

responseBody.description: The role after its permission set has been updated.

parameters.description: Identifier of the role within the current organization.
parameters.name: roleId

requestBody.description: The new permission set to assign to the role.

prerequisites.description: A role must already exist in the current organization before its permission set can be updated.

operations.description:
Remove a permission assignment from a role.

This operation permanently removes a single permission link from an organization role. It is used when an organization owner edits a custom role's access set and no longer wants that permission attached to the role.

The role context is required because permissions belong to a specific role within the organization. The target permission assignment must exist under the given role, and the server should reject the request if the association does not belong to that role or if the role cannot be modified by the current member.

Built-in roles are protected by role business rules, so the service must prevent modifications that would violate the organization access model. If the role-permission assignment cannot be found, return a not-found error. If the caller lacks role management authority, return a forbidden error.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the role by roleId within the current organization context and verify the caller has permission to manage roles. Then load the role-permission association by rolePermissionId constrained to the same role. Reject the request if the association does not belong to the specified role or if the role is built-in and protected by business rules that forbid modifying its permission set in this way.

Delete the role-permission row in a transaction. No cascading delete should be needed beyond removing the association record itself. If the schema uses organization-scoped role ownership, ensure the role also belongs to the active organization before deleting. Return not found when either the role or the association does not exist in scope, and return forbidden when the caller lacks access. Do not expose any response payload.

parameters.description: Identifier of the role within the current organization scope.
parameters.name: roleId

parameters.description: Identifier of the role-permission association to remove from the specified role.
parameters.name: rolePermissionId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of projects within the currently selected organization.

This endpoint is used to browse project records that belong to the active organization context. It supports filtering and sorting so users can quickly find projects by status or other list criteria, while preserving strict tenant isolation between organizations.

Access is limited to members who have permission to view projects in the selected organization. The response is intended for project overviews and list pages, and includes summary data suitable for displaying project identity and status in UI tables or cards.

If the caller does not have project view permission, the request must be rejected. If the selected organization context is missing or invalid, the request must also be rejected. Results must never include projects from another organization.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Read projects from erp_hrm_time_projects constrained to the current organization context from the authenticated member session. Apply permission checks for project:view before querying.

Support pagination, keyword search, status filtering, and stable sorting in the request body. Every query must be scoped by organization id, and any status filter must not cross tenant boundaries. Return only summary fields needed for browsing, including project identity, display metadata, and lifecycle status.

Sort by a deterministic default when the client does not specify sort order. Reject requests with invalid filters, unsupported sort fields, or missing organization context. If the underlying project schema includes visual distinction data such as color, include it in summary projection if available. Use a paginated response DTO named IPageIErpHrmTimeProject.ISummary.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of project summaries for the active organization.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, pagination, and sorting criteria for browsing projects in the current organization.

operations.description:
Create a new project in the current organization.

This operation allows authorized users to register a project that will be used for planning, task management, and time tracking. The project belongs to the currently selected organization and must be created with a valid display color so it can be visually distinguished in project lists and work views.

Projects are organization-scoped records. The created project can later be assigned employees through project memberships, receive tasks, and accumulate timelog entries. The status, budget, and schedule fields define the project’s operational state and planning context. If the caller does not have permission to manage projects, the request must be rejected.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Validate that the caller has project management permission in the current organization context.
Insert a new row into erp_hrm_time_projects using the selected organization scope and the submitted project attributes.
Enforce required field validation for the project identity and visual color code, and validate any status or date fields according to the project business rules.
Prevent cross-organization creation by binding the record to the active organization only; never accept an organization identifier from the client body.
Return the newly created project entity after persistence. If downstream rules reject the project state or required fields are invalid, surface a validation error. If authorization is missing, return a forbidden response.

responseBody.description: The newly created project record.

requestBody.description: Project data to create within the current organization.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single project within the currently selected organization.

This operation returns the full project record for viewing project details, including the project’s identity, display metadata, lifecycle status, schedule, and budget information. It is intended for project detail screens and other workflows that need the complete project entity rather than a list summary.

Access is limited to users who can view projects in the active organization context. The project must belong to the selected organization, and requests for projects outside that organization must be rejected. This protects tenant isolation while still allowing project members and authorized managers to inspect project information.

If the project does not exist in the selected organization, the service must return a not-found response. If the caller lacks project visibility in the current organization, the service must reject the request with an authorization error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the project by projectId and the currently selected organization scope in a single lookup. Verify that the caller has project:view permission in the active organization context before returning data.

Query erp_hrm_time_projects by primary identifier and organization boundary. Do not return a project from another organization even if the identifier matches. Map the entity fields directly from the table, including name, description, color code, status, budget hours, start date, and end date, along with any other actual project columns present in the schema.

Return 404 when the project is not found within the current organization. Return 403 when the caller lacks permission. The endpoint has no request body and must not perform pagination or filtering.

responseBody.description: The full project record for the requested project.

parameters.description: The project identifier within the current organization scope.
parameters.name: projectId

operations.description:
Update an existing project in the selected organization.

This operation allows project managers to edit the project’s name, description, color code, status, budget hours, and planning dates. It supports ongoing project maintenance so teams can keep project identity, schedule, and visual presentation current while work is in progress.

The project belongs to a single organization, so the update is always applied within the caller’s current organization context. The project color code is used for visual distinction in the user interface, and planning fields such as description, budget hours, start date, and end date are optional business details that help with planning and tracking.

The server must reject updates when the caller lacks project management permission, when the project does not exist in the current organization, or when the requested status change violates project lifecycle rules. The updated project is returned after persistence so clients can refresh any project lists, details, or dashboards that depend on the changed data.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the project by projectId within the current organization context. Verify the caller has project management permission.

Apply only mutable fields from the request body to the project record. Validate required fields such as name and color code when they are present in the update payload, and preserve existing values for omitted optional fields according to the update DTO semantics.

Enforce organization isolation so the project must belong to the caller’s selected organization. Reject the request with not found if the project does not exist in that organization.

Validate lifecycle status transitions against the project business rules. Allow updates to active, archived, or completed only when the transition is permitted by the project workflow. Do not allow any change that would conflict with the rule that archived and completed projects remain viewable but cannot receive new timelogs.

Persist the updated project in a transaction. Return the full updated project entity. If downstream invariants are enforced at the service layer, ensure any invalid combination of schedule, status, or display fields is rejected with a clear validation error.

responseBody.description: The updated project record after the changes have been saved.

parameters.description: The project identifier within the current organization.
parameters.name: projectId

requestBody.description: Fields that can be updated on the project.

operations.description:
Permanently deletes a project from the current organization when deletion rules are satisfied.

This operation is intended for project management workflows where a project is no longer needed and has no recorded work history. A project can only be removed if it belongs to the active organization context and does not have any associated timelogs. This protects historical time data from being lost and ensures cross-tenant isolation is preserved.

The caller must have project management authority in the current organization. If the project still has timelogs, the request must be rejected. If the project does not exist in the current organization context, the request must fail as not found. Successful deletion removes the project record and any project-local associations that are deleted together by the persistence layer, while preserving unrelated organization data.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the project by projectId within the active organization context. Verify that the caller has project management permission in the current organization.

Before deleting, check for any timelog records referencing the project. If at least one timelog exists, reject the request with a conflict-style error and do not delete the project. If the project is missing in the current organization context, return not found.

Perform the delete in a transaction to avoid race conditions between the pre-check and deletion. Ensure the deletion respects organization isolation so a project from another organization cannot be removed even if the identifier is known. Return the deleted project representation if the service layer convention expects a body for successful destructive operations; otherwise return no content.

parameters.description: The identifier of the project to permanently delete within the current organization context.
parameters.name: projectId

operations.description:
Retrieve the list of employees assigned to a project.

This operation returns the current project team composition for the specified project, including each employee's membership record and assignment role within that project. It is used to browse who participates in the project and to distinguish between general members and project leads.

The result is scoped to the selected project and therefore reflects only the memberships belonging to that project. It supports paginated browsing for project staffing screens and should be used together with project detail and membership management operations when viewing or maintaining the team structure.

If the project does not exist or the caller is not allowed to view project membership data, the request must be rejected. The response should remain consistent with the project's current memberships and should not include employees from other projects.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_time_project_memberships for the given erp_hrm_time_project_id.
Join the employee relation so the list can be presented as project team composition, but keep the primary response focused on membership records. Apply pagination and any supported search/sort filters in the request body according to list browsing conventions.

Enforce that the target project exists and belongs to the current organization context before querying. Reject access when the caller lacks project visibility or management rights. Preserve the unique project-employee constraint already enforced by the database; this operation is read-only and must not create or modify memberships.

Use the project_role field as the assignment role for each row. Include employee-linked summary data only if the corresponding summary DTO exists in the component model; otherwise, return the membership entity/summary shape that matches the generated schema. Handle empty results by returning an empty page rather than an error.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of project membership summaries for the specified project.

parameters.description: Project identifier within the current organization scope.
parameters.name: projectId

requestBody.description: Pagination, search, and sorting criteria for browsing memberships in a project.

operations.description:
Create a project membership for an employee within the selected project.

This operation assigns one employee to one project and records the employee's role within that project team, such as a regular member or project lead. It is used for project staffing and for determining who is eligible to participate in project work and task management within the project scope.

The project membership is organization-scoped through the selected organization context. The project identified by `{projectId}` and the employee referenced in the request must both belong to the same organization, and the employee must not already be assigned to the project. If the project or employee cannot be resolved in the current organization, or if the membership already exists, the request must be rejected.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target project by id within the current organization context and verify that it exists. Validate that the request employee belongs to the same organization and that the employee is eligible to be added to the project.

Check the unique constraint on (erp_hrm_time_project_id, erp_hrm_time_employee_id) before inserting. If a membership already exists for the employee and project pair, return a conflict-style validation error and do not create a duplicate row.

Persist a new erp_hrm_time_project_memberships row using the path projectId, the requested employee id, and the requested project_role. The service should create the record in a transaction so concurrent duplicate assignments cannot bypass the uniqueness rule. Return the created membership with its linked project and employee context if the API layer uses entity expansion.

If the organization context is missing, the project is not accessible, the employee does not belong to the same organization, or the provided role value is invalid, reject the request with a clear business error.

responseBody.description: The newly created project membership, including the assigned employee and project assignment details.

parameters.description: Identifier of the project within the current organization.
parameters.name: projectId

requestBody.description: Project membership creation payload. Provide the employee to assign and the role they will hold in the project team.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single project membership for a specific project.

This operation returns the employee assignment record that connects one employee to one project and identifies the employee's role within that project team, such as member or project lead. It is useful for viewing the current composition of a project team and confirming who is assigned to participate in the project.

The membership is always resolved within the selected organization and the specified project. If the project or membership does not exist in the current organization, or if the membership does not belong to the specified project, the request must fail with an appropriate not-found response. Access must also respect the platform's project visibility and management permissions.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the project by projectId within the current organization context, then load the project membership by membershipId constrained to that same project. Verify that the membership belongs to the project and that the project itself belongs to the selected organization. Return the full project membership entity including its employee and assigned project role fields as defined by the schema.

Do not allow cross-organization access. If either the project or membership is missing, or if the membership is associated with a different project, respond with a 404-style not-found error. This endpoint is read-only and must not modify membership data. Authorization should allow users with project viewing capability and users with project management capability, according to the organization permission model.

responseBody.description: The project membership record for the specified project.

parameters.description: The identifier of the project within the current organization.
parameters.name: projectId

operations.description:
Remove an employee from a project by deleting the project membership record.

This operation ends the association between one employee and one project inside the currently selected organization. It is intended for project staffing changes, team restructuring, and lead reassignment workflows. Because project memberships are independent, removing one membership does not affect the employee's assignments to other projects.

Only users with project management permission may perform this action. The membership must belong to the project identified in the path, and the project must be accessible in the current organization context. If the membership does not exist, does not belong to the specified project, or the caller lacks permission, the request is rejected. If the removed employee was marked as a project lead for that project, the project leadership capability for that specific project ends immediately.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the target project membership by membershipId, ensuring it belongs to projectId and to the current organization context.
Verify the caller has project management permission in the current organization.
Reject the request with not found if the membership does not exist or is not attached to the specified project.
Delete the membership record only; do not touch any other memberships for the same employee.
After deletion, the employee must no longer be considered assigned to that project, and any project-lead flag for that membership is implicitly revoked by removal.
Do not cascade-delete employee, project, task, or timelog records.
Return the deleted membership representation so the client can refresh local team state. Handle concurrent deletion safely by treating already-removed memberships as not found.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of tasks for a specific project.

This operation returns the tasks that belong to the selected project and supports browsing work items by status, priority, assignee, and due date. It is intended for users who need to review and manage task progress inside the current project context.

The task list is scoped by project and must only include records from that project. Filtering and pagination apply within the project boundary, and the response is optimized for list views rather than full task details. The task title, description, status, priority, estimated hours, and due date are core task fields that shape list browsing and planning behavior.

If the project does not exist, or the caller lacks permission to view tasks in the project, the service must return an appropriate authorization or not-found error. Invalid filter values, malformed pagination settings, or attempts to query outside the project scope should be rejected before executing the database query.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the project by projectId and verify the caller has access to the project within the current organization context.
Use the task table as the primary source and filter rows by the project foreign key.
Apply optional filters from the request body for status, priority, and assigned employee; combine them with pagination and sorting rules from the list-search contract.
Return tasks ordered according to the requested sort fields when provided, otherwise apply a stable default order suitable for task browsing.
Join only what is necessary for summary output, avoiding expensive detail joins unless required by the summary DTO.
Ensure assignee filters respect project scope and do not return tasks assigned to employees outside the selected organization.
Reject invalid enum values, negative pagination values, or unsupported sort fields with a validation error.
If the project is missing, return not found. If the user cannot view the project or tasks within it, return forbidden.
Use the paginated response wrapper for task summaries.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of task summaries for the selected project.

parameters.description: The project identifier within the current organization scope.

operations.description:
Create a new task within a project.

This operation creates a project work item inside the selected project context. A task belongs to exactly one project, starts in the open status by default, and may include a description, priority, estimated hours, due date, an assigned employee, and a parent task for one-level subtask nesting.

The assigned employee, when provided, must be a member of the same project. The parent task, when provided, must also belong to the same project. Only users with project management permission or project-lead authority for this project can create tasks here.

If the project is not eligible for task creation, or if the assigned employee or parent task does not match the project scope, the request must be rejected with a validation error.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target project by id within the current organization context and verify that it exists and is not deleted. Enforce authorization so only users with project:manage permission or a project-lead membership for the same project can create tasks.

Validate the request body against the task creation rules: title is required; description, estimated_hours, due_date, assigned employee, and parent task are optional; priority must be one of the supported task priorities; the new task status must be set to open regardless of client input. If an assigned employee id is provided, confirm that the employee is assigned to the same project through erp_hrm_time_project_memberships. If a parent task id is provided, confirm that it belongs to the same project and that the nesting depth does not exceed one level.

Persist the task in erp_hrm_time_tasks with the project foreign key, optional employee and parent_task references, and audit timestamps. Do not create history entries here unless the implementation layer explicitly records status creation events elsewhere. Return the created task entity. Reject requests for missing project, invalid scope, unauthorized access, invalid assignment, or invalid parent task with the appropriate domain error.

responseBody.description: The newly created task, including its project context and current state.

parameters.description: The project identifier for the project that will own the new task.
parameters.name: projectId

operations.description:
Retrieve a single task within a project.

This operation returns the full task record for the specified project and task identifiers, including the task title, description, current status, priority, estimated effort, due date, and assigned employee reference. Tasks are always scoped to a project, so the project path parameter is required to resolve the task in the correct project context.

The task entity also supports a one-level parent task relationship for subtasks. Consumers can use this endpoint to inspect a task’s current state and its assignment within the project. Access must respect the caller’s organization context and project visibility rules, and the task must belong to the given project.

If the task does not exist, does not belong to the specified project, or is not accessible in the current organization context, the request should fail with the appropriate not-found or authorization error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the task by project scope first, then resolve the task by its id within the same organization. Verify that the task belongs to the given project before returning it.

Use a join or relation load against erp_hrm_time_projects and erp_hrm_time_tasks to ensure the path projectId and taskId refer to the same organization-scoped project/task pair. Return the full task record fields defined in erp_hrm_time_tasks: id, erp_hrm_time_project_id, erp_hrm_time_employee_id, parent_task_id, title, description, status, priority, estimated_hours, due_date, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at.

Do not include child task collections in the response. If the task is not found under the specified project, return 404. If the caller lacks access to the organization or project, return the standard authorization error.

responseBody.description: Full task details for the specified project task.

operations.description:
Update a task that belongs to a specific project.

This endpoint lets authorized users edit task details within the context of a single project. A task may include a title, description, status, priority, estimated hours, due date, assigned employee, and parent task. The task remains scoped to the project identified in the path, and any assigned employee must be a member of that same project.

Task status changes are tracked as part of the task history, so consumers should expect the system to record status transitions when the status value changes. The endpoint also preserves the one-level subtask structure by allowing a parent task only within the same project.

Authorization is limited to users who can manage the project or act as a project lead for that project. Validation errors are returned when the task does not exist, the project context does not match, the assigned employee is not part of the project, the parent task is invalid, or the caller lacks sufficient permission.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the task by projectId and taskId in the same query scope to ensure the task belongs to the specified project. Verify organization context from the authenticated member before any modification.

Authorize if the caller has project:manage permission or is a project lead for the target project. Reject access if neither condition is met.

Validate update payload fields against task business rules: title is required for persisted state, status must be one of the allowed task states, priority must be one of the allowed values, estimated hours and due date are optional, and description may be null or empty depending on DTO definition. If assigned employee is provided, confirm the employee belongs to the same project. If parent task is provided, confirm it exists, belongs to the same project, and does not create deeper nesting beyond one level.

If status changes, write a task history entry capturing the previous status, new status, timestamp, and acting user. Use a transaction so the task update and history insert succeed or fail together.

Return not found when the task does not exist within the specified project. Return validation errors for invalid assignee/parent relationships. Return forbidden for insufficient permissions. Preserve all other fields not included in the update request.

responseBody.description: The updated task after applying the changes.

operations.description:
Permanently removes a task from a project.

This operation is used to delete a project task within the current organization context. The task must belong to the project identified by `projectId`, and the caller must have permission to manage tasks in that project. Tasks may be part of a project hierarchy and may have history entries, so the service must validate project ownership before deletion and reject attempts to delete a task that does not belong to the specified project.

Deletion is intended for project-managed work items and affects only the targeted task record. Related behavior such as task history visibility, subtasks, and any downstream business rules must be enforced by the service layer according to project and task constraints. If the task cannot be deleted because it is protected by domain rules or the identifiers do not match, the request must fail with an appropriate error.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the project by projectId within the current organization context and verify that the caller is authorized to manage tasks for that project. Then load the task by taskId and confirm it belongs to the specified project. If the task does not exist, return not found. If the task exists but belongs to a different project or organization, return not found or forbidden according to the service's access policy.

Delete the task record using a transaction-safe operation. If the database enforces foreign key constraints from child subtasks or history records, the implementation must rely on the existing domain rules for task deletion and surface a business error when deletion is not allowed. Do not accept a request body. Return success with no content on completion.

operations.description:
Retrieve the status-change history for a specific task within a project.

This operation returns the immutable audit trail of task status transitions, including the time of each change, the previous status, the new status, and the member who made the update. It is intended for project members, project leads, and users with project management privileges who need to review how a task evolved over time.

The history is scoped to the selected organization, the specified project, and the specified task. If the caller cannot access the parent project or the task does not belong to the provided project, the request is rejected. Because history entries are part of the audit record, this endpoint is read-only and only supports browsing through paginated results.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load task history entries for the given project and task, ensuring the task belongs to the provided project and both belong to the current organization context. Use the task history entries table as an immutable source of status transition records. Apply pagination, sorting by recorded timestamp descending by default, and return a paginated summary payload.

Do not allow modification of history data. If the task is not found in the current organization or does not belong to the provided project, return a not-found or forbidden-style error according to the service convention. If the caller lacks permission to view tasks in the project, reject the request. The response must include only fields needed for list rendering, such as timestamp, previous status, new status, and actor reference, while preserving the audit trail integrity.

responseBody.description: Paginated task history entries for the requested task.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single task history entry for a task within a project.

This operation returns the immutable audit record that was created when a task status changed. The record is scoped to the specified project and task, so consumers can inspect the exact change history for a task without mixing entries from other tasks, projects, or organizations.

The returned history entry preserves the original timestamp, the previous status, the new status, and the user who made the change. Because task history is part of the audit trail, this endpoint is read-only and is intended for task detail screens, project activity views, and administrative review workflows.

The request is authorized within the currently selected organization context. If the project, task, or history entry does not exist in that scope, or if the caller is not allowed to view the project task data, the service must respond with an appropriate not-found or forbidden error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Resolve the current organization from the authenticated member context, then verify that the project belongs to that organization and that the task belongs to the specified project. After that, load the history entry by its identifier while enforcing that it belongs to the specified task.

Use a single read query with joins or equivalent repository checks to ensure the project-task-history hierarchy is consistent before returning data. Do not allow history entries to be fetched across projects or organizations. The entry is immutable, so no update logic applies.

Return 404 when the project, task, or history entry is missing or not linked through the specified hierarchy. Return 403 when the caller lacks permission to view the task/project scope. The response should include the full history entry entity as defined by the task history schema, including the stored status transition metadata and actor information. Keep the endpoint read-only and do not expose any mutation behavior.

responseBody.description: The full task history entry for the specified project task.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of timelogs for the current organization context.

This operation supports browsing daily work entries that record the date, duration, project, optional task, optional description, and billable status of each time entry. Timelogs are organization-scoped and are always filtered to the caller's selected organization. Depending on permissions, the response may include only the caller's own timelogs or all employees' timelogs in the organization.

The list supports filtering by date range, project, task, and billable status, along with pagination and sorting for efficient review. Use this endpoint to power employee time-entry screens, manager review pages, and organization-wide timelog searches.

Access is subject to permission checks and data visibility rules. Locked timelogs that belong to approved timesheets remain visible but are not editable through update or delete operations. Archived or completed projects may still appear in historical results, but they do not accept new entries.

Return validation errors when the search criteria are malformed, the organization context is missing, or the caller lacks the required visibility permission.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_time_timelogs within the active organization context only. Enforce member ownership restrictions unless the caller has time:view_all permission, in which case include all employees' timelogs for the organization. Support pagination, search filters, and sorting in the request body. Expected filters: date range, project, task, and billable flag. Joins may be required to resolve project/task scoping and to ensure returned rows belong to the active organization. Exclude data from other organizations at the query level.

Return a paginated summary projection ordered by the requested sort criteria, with sensible defaults such as most recent date first and stable tie-breaking by primary key. Validate that task filters belong to the selected project when both are supplied. Validate all referenced identifiers exist within the caller's organization. If the caller is not permitted to view other employees' timelogs, constrain the query to the authenticated employee only. Reject invalid page, size, and sorting parameters with standard validation errors.

responseBody.description: Paginated timelog summaries for the current organization context.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, pagination, and sorting options for timelog browsing.

operations.description:
Create a new timelog entry for the current organization and employee.

This operation records a single day-based work entry with the selected project, optional task, logged duration, optional description, and billable flag. Timelogs are the base unit of time tracking and are used later in weekly timesheets, reporting, and timer conversion workflows.

The created timelog is always scoped to the authenticated employee in the current organization context. The service must validate that the selected project belongs to the same organization, that any provided task belongs to that project, and that the employee is allowed to create time entries. Existing locked or approved timesheet rules must be enforced so protected records cannot be altered through this endpoint.

If the target project is archived or completed, the request must be rejected. The operation should also ensure the employee is active, the work date is valid, and the duration is a positive value in minutes. On success, return the created timelog with its persisted identifiers and timestamps.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Insert a new row into erp_hrm_time_timelogs using the authenticated member as erp_hrm_time_member_id and the current organization-scoped employee as the owner context.
Validate that the employee belongs to the active organization and is active, that the project belongs to the same organization and is not archived or completed, and that any task belongs to the same project.
Use the provided work date, duration minutes, description, and billable flag; do not accept ownership overrides from the request body.
If the timelog is created from a running timer workflow, the timer conversion should be handled elsewhere; this endpoint only creates a manual timelog.
Emit any required activity log entry according to business rules after successful insert. Return the created entity with timestamps. Reject with a validation or conflict error when organization scope, project/task integrity, or employee status rules are violated.

responseBody.description: The newly created timelog record.

requestBody.description: Timelog creation details for the current employee in the selected organization.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single timelog entry by its identifier.

This operation returns the full timelog record, including the employee who created it, the project it belongs to, the optional task association, the work date, duration, billable flag, description, and audit timestamps. It is intended for viewing a specific time entry in detail after selecting the current organization context.

Access to the record is limited by organization scope and by the caller's permissions. Ordinary employees can retrieve their own timelogs, while users with broader time-tracking visibility can retrieve timelogs across the selected organization. If the timelog does not exist in the current organization, or the caller is not allowed to view it, the request must fail with an appropriate not-found or forbidden response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the timelog by primary key and eagerly validate organization scope through its related member, project, and optional task associations. Ensure the resolved timelog belongs to the caller's selected organization before returning it.

Return the full entity with its direct fields. Do not expose timelogs from other organizations. If the record is missing, or the caller lacks permission to view it, return an authorization-appropriate error. Preserve deleted records according to existing service policy only if they are still intended to be retrievable; otherwise treat deleted_at as hidden from normal reads.

No complex filtering or pagination is needed. This is a single-entity lookup, so use a straightforward read-by-id query with relation checks and consistent error handling.

responseBody.description: The full timelog record for the requested entry.

parameters.description: Identifier of the timelog to retrieve (UUID).
parameters.name: timelogId

operations.description:
Update an existing timelog entry.

This operation allows an employee or an authorized manager to modify a single time entry within the currently selected organization. A timelog records the work date, logged duration in minutes, optional description, billable flag, and the project and optional task associated with the work.

The server must validate that the timelog belongs to the current organization context, that the referenced project and task remain valid, and that the task belongs to the selected project when present.
