Access should follow the project's view permissions, and the service must reject requests that fall outside the caller's organization or authorization scope. Because task history entries are append-only records, this operation is strictly read-only and does not support modification.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the project by id within the current organization scope and verify project-view access before querying history. Resolve task history through erp_hrm_time_task_history_entries joined to erp_hrm_time_tasks, filtering only tasks whose erp_hrm_time_project_id matches the requested project. Return paginated results ordered by changed_at descending, with a stable secondary order by id to keep pagination consistent.

Do not cross organization boundaries in any join or filter. If the project does not exist in the current organization, return not found. If the caller lacks access, return forbidden or the application's standard access-denied response. The endpoint is read-only and must never expose update or delete behavior.

responseBody.description: Paginated task status history entries for the specified project.

parameters.description: Project identifier within the currently selected organization.
parameters.name: projectId

requestBody.description: Pagination and filtering criteria for project task history browsing.

operations.description:
Retrieve the full status-change history for a task within a project.

This operation returns the recorded lifecycle trail for the selected task, showing each historical change in chronological order. It is intended for accountability and review, allowing users to see when the task moved from one status to another and who performed the change.

The task history is an immutable audit-style record. Each entry belongs to exactly one task and one project scope, and the returned data must not include entries from other tasks or other projects. If the task does not exist, does not belong to the specified project, or is not visible in the current organization context, the request should fail with a not-found or access-related error as appropriate.

Because the history is append-only, this endpoint only reads the stored trail and does not allow editing or deletion of historical entries.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the project and task by the supplied identifiers and verify that the task belongs to the project and current organization context before querying history.

Query erp_hrm_time_task_history_entries filtered by the task reference, ordered by recorded timestamp ascending so the consumer can reconstruct the lifecycle sequence. Return all immutable history entries for the task, including the old status, new status, timestamp, and actor responsible for the change.

Do not join or expose unrelated task records. Do not allow any mutation behavior in this endpoint. If the project or task cannot be resolved within the current tenant scope, return a not-found response. If the caller lacks permission to view the project/task, return the standard authorization error for the service.

responseBody.description: The ordered task history trail for the selected task.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the project that owns the task.
parameters.name: projectId

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the task whose history is being retrieved.
parameters.name: taskId

operations.description:
Start a live timer for the current employee.

This operation creates a running time-tracking session tied to the selected project in the current organization. The timer captures the work context from the beginning, including the optional task and a short description of the work being performed, so the session can later be stopped and converted into a timelog.

The selected project must belong to the current organization, and any provided task must belong to that project. The system also enforces that each employee can have only one active timer at a time, and deactivated employees cannot start a timer. If validation fails, the request is rejected and no running session is created.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new running timer for the authenticated member's employee in the current organization.

Resolve the employee from the authenticated member and selected organization context, then verify the employee is active. Reject the request if the employee has an existing active timer because only one timer may run per employee. Verify the target project exists in the same organization and is eligible for timer tracking. If taskId is supplied, verify the task exists, belongs to the same project, and belongs to the same organization through the project relationship.

Insert a new erp_hrm_time_timers row with member_id, employee_id, project_id, optional task_id, started_at, description, created_at, and updated_at. started_at must be the current timestamp. Do not create any timelog here; timelog creation happens only when the timer is stopped. Return the created timer record with its relations as needed by the Timer response schema.

Handle conflicts and invalid references explicitly: active timer conflict, inactive employee, missing project, project/task scope mismatch, and organization scope mismatch. Because this is a create operation, use standard transactional behavior to ensure no duplicate active timer is inserted under concurrent requests.

responseBody.description: The newly started running timer session.

requestBody.description: Timer start data for the current employee.

prerequisites.description: A timer can only start against an existing project in the current organization, so the project must be created before the timer can reference it.

operations.description:
Stop the currently running timer and convert it into a completed timelog.

This operation ends the employee’s active live work session in the currently selected organization. When the timer is stopped, the system calculates the elapsed duration, rounds it to the nearest minute, and creates a timelog that preserves the timer’s work context, including the recorded start timestamp, project, task, and description.

The endpoint is part of the time-tracking workflow for members who are actively tracking work in real time. It enforces organization isolation and employee activity status, so requests are rejected when the caller has no active timer, the timer belongs to another organization, or the employee is deactivated. If the timer cannot be stopped for business reasons, the service must return a validation or conflict error instead of creating a timelog.
operations.name: stop
operations.specification:
Resolve the caller’s current organization context and active employee identity from the authenticated session.
Load the active timer for that employee within the selected organization only. If no active timer exists, return a conflict or not-found style error consistent with the service conventions.

Before stopping, verify the employee is still active and that the timer belongs to the current organization. Reject the request if the timer is outside scope or the employee is deactivated.

Compute the elapsed duration from the timer’s start timestamp to the stop moment, round the result to the nearest minute, and persist a new timelog using the timer’s stored work context. The created timelog must inherit the timer’s project, optional task, and description, and it should capture the timer’s start timestamp as the beginning of the work session.

Perform the timer stop and timelog creation atomically in a transaction so partial updates cannot occur. After successful creation, mark the timer as stopped/consumed according to the existing persistence model and return the created timelog entity. If the timer has already been stopped concurrently, fail safely with a conflict error.

responseBody.description: The completed timelog created from the stopped timer.

operations.description:
Discard the current running timer for the active employee.

This operation ends a live time-tracking session without creating a timelog. It is intended for employees who started tracking time but decide not to convert the running session into a recorded time entry. The discarded timer is removed immediately and can no longer be edited, stopped, or resumed.

The request is evaluated in the current organization context and against the authenticated employee's own timer. The system rejects the action if the employee does not have an active timer, if the employee is deactivated, or if another business rule prevents timer actions in the current state. Because discarding does not produce a timelog, no reporting or timesheet data is generated from the discarded session.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Resolve the authenticated member's employee record in the selected organization context, then fetch the employee's currently active timer. If no active timer exists, return a not-found or conflict-style error consistent with timer workflows.

Before deleting, verify the employee is active. If the employee has been deactivated, block the request.

Perform a transactional delete of the timer row only. Do not create a timelog, do not update timesheets, and do not emit any duration calculation. This endpoint must not affect other timers because the domain allows only one active timer per employee.

Apply organization isolation so the employee can only discard a timer inside the current selected organization. If the timer belongs to a different organization context, reject the request. After deletion, return success with no body.

operations.description:
Retrieve the timer that is currently running for the authenticated employee.

This endpoint lets a member confirm whether live time tracking is active in the current organization context and inspect the running session details, including its associated project, optional task, description, and start time.

If the employee has no active timer, the request should be handled as a read of an absent current timer according to the service’s standard not-found behavior for singleton resources. The endpoint only exposes the timer for the currently authenticated member and does not allow access to other employees’ running sessions.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the authenticated member and current organization context from the request. Resolve the active timer for that employee by querying erp_hrm_time_timers for the row whose employee ownership matches the current member and whose running state indicates it is active.

Return the full timer entity with its current project, optional task, start timestamp, and description fields. Do not create, modify, or stop the timer in this operation. If no active timer exists for the employee, respond with the service’s standard 404/not-found handling for singleton current-resource reads.

Enforce organization isolation through the current context before querying. Ensure the response never leaks another employee’s timer. Since this is a read-only singleton endpoint, there is no pagination, filtering, or request body.

responseBody.description: The currently running timer for the authenticated employee.

operations.description:
Create a draft timesheet for a specific week.

This operation creates the editable weekly timesheet record for the currently selected organization and authenticated employee. When the draft is created, the system automatically includes all timelogs for that employee that fall within the selected week, so the employee can review and adjust the weekly record before submission.

A draft timesheet belongs to exactly one employee and one Monday-to-Sunday week. The created record remains in draft status until it is submitted for approval. If another timesheet already exists for the same employee and week, the request must fail to preserve the one-timesheet-per-week rule. The service must also ensure the target week is valid and that the employee is allowed to manage their own timesheet within the current organization context.

If the employee has no timelogs in the selected week, the draft may still be created if the business workflow allows it for later manual addition; however, submission will remain blocked until at least one timelog is included. Any validation error such as an invalid week boundary or duplicate weekly timesheet should be returned clearly to the client.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Resolve the authenticated member and the currently selected organization, then resolve the employee record that owns timesheets in that organization. Validate that the requested week start date is a Monday and compute the matching week end date as Sunday of the same week.

Check for an existing non-deleted timesheet for the same employee and week_start_date using the unique constraint on erp_hrm_time_timesheets. If one exists, reject the request with a conflict error. Create the timesheet row with status draft and null submitted_at, reviewed_at, reviewed_by_member_id, and rejection_reason. Persist the row first, then fetch all timelogs for the employee whose work_date falls within the week range and create join rows in erp_hrm_time_timesheet_timelogs for each matching timelog, avoiding duplicates through the unique constraint on the join table.

Run the create and join-row inserts in a transaction so the draft and its included timelogs stay consistent. Scope all queries to the current organization through the employee relation, and ensure only the current employee's own timesheets can be created. Return the created timesheet entity with its identifiers and current lifecycle fields. Do not attempt to modify locked approved timesheets or existing submitted/reviewed records, and do not create duplicate join rows if the draft is regenerated in an idempotent retry scenario.

responseBody.description: The created draft timesheet with its current lifecycle state and weekly ownership metadata.

requestBody.description: Draft timesheet creation payload containing the target week for the currently selected employee.

operations.description:
Submit a draft timesheet for approval.

This operation changes a weekly timesheet from draft to submitted so it can be reviewed by users with approval permission. The timesheet remains owned by the same employee and tied to the same weekly period after submission.

Only the employee who owns the timesheet, or a user with approval permissions in the selected organization context, may perform this action according to the organization’s access rules. The service must reject submissions for locked, already submitted, approved, or otherwise invalid timesheets, and it must preserve the timesheet’s existing timelogs and week boundaries when the status changes.
operations.name: submit
operations.specification:
Load the target timesheet by id within the current organization context and verify that it belongs to the active organization. Confirm the requester is either the timesheet owner or has the appropriate approval/management permission required by the domain rules.

Validate that the timesheet is currently in draft status. Reject the request if it is already submitted, approved, or otherwise not editable. Reject if the timesheet has no included timelogs, because submission requires at least one timelog. Reject if the employee is deactivated, because deactivated employees cannot submit timesheets.

When valid, update the timesheet status from draft to submitted and set the submitted timestamp to the current time. Preserve the week start/end dates, owner, and existing timelog links. If the implementation stores submission metadata on the timesheet, persist it in the same transaction. The operation should be idempotent only in the sense that a repeated submit on a non-draft timesheet must fail with a domain validation error rather than silently reapplying the transition.

Return the updated timesheet entity after commit. Use transactional integrity so that status changes and any related submission metadata are written atomically. Surface not-found, forbidden, and domain validation failures with appropriate HTTP errors.

responseBody.description: The submitted timesheet after its status changes to submitted.

parameters.description: The timesheet identifier within the current organization context.
parameters.name: timesheetId

prerequisites.description: A weekly timesheet draft must exist before it can be submitted for approval.

operations.description:
Approve a submitted timesheet for the current organization.

This operation is available only to users with timesheet approval permission. It finalizes a weekly timesheet that is already in submitted status and returns the approved record so the client can refresh the reviewer-facing view.

After approval, the included timelogs are locked because the weekly time record is finalized. Requests must be rejected when the timesheet is not submitted, belongs to a different organization, or the caller does not have approval permission.
operations.name: approve
operations.specification:
Load the target timesheet by ID within the authenticated member's selected organization. Verify that the caller has the time approval permission and that the timesheet status is submitted. Reject the request with a forbidden or conflict-style error if the user lacks permission, the timesheet is outside the current organization, or the status is not submitted.

On success, update the timesheet status from submitted to approved and persist the review timestamp and reviewer reference if those fields exist in the schema. Then lock all timelogs associated with the timesheet through the join table so they cannot be edited or deleted afterward. Perform the status update and locking in a transaction to avoid partial approval states. Return the refreshed timesheet entity after the update.

If the data model includes a dedicated relation for reviewed-by or reviewed-at, populate it from the current member context and current timestamp. If the schema does not expose review metadata fields, only change the status and apply the locking side effects defined by the timesheet-timelog relationship.

responseBody.description: The approved timesheet after the approval action has been applied.

parameters.description: Identifier of the timesheet to approve within the current organization.
parameters.name: timesheetId

operations.description:
Reject a submitted timesheet with a required reason.

This operation is used by an approver to review a submitted weekly timesheet and send it back to the employee for correction. A rejection is only valid when the timesheet is currently in submitted status and belongs to the selected organization context. The rejection reason is mandatory so the employee understands what must be fixed before resubmission.

When the rejection is accepted, the timesheet returns to draft status and remains editable by its owner. The reviewed timestamp and reviewer reference are updated as part of the review workflow, and the included timelogs remain associated with the same weekly timesheet so the employee can revise and resubmit it. Requests for draft, approved, or already rejected timesheets must be rejected.

Access is limited to users with timesheet approval permission. If the user lacks permission, if the timesheet is outside the current organization, or if the target timesheet is not eligible for rejection, the request must fail with an appropriate validation or authorization error.
operations.name: reject
operations.specification:
Load the target timesheet by ID within the current organization scope. Verify that the authenticated member has approval permission. Reject the request if the timesheet does not belong to the active organization, if it is not in submitted status, or if it is already approved or rejected.

Validate the request body to require a non-empty rejection reason. Persist the status transition from submitted to draft and store the reviewer/review metadata according to the timesheet schema. Keep the included timelogs linked to the timesheet; do not remove them during rejection.

The operation should be transactional so that status, review metadata, and any related audit/event side effects are saved together. Return the updated timesheet entity after persistence. If the record is missing, return not found. If the status is not eligible, return a domain validation error.

responseBody.description: The updated timesheet after rejection, returned in draft status with review metadata applied.

parameters.description: The timesheet identifier within the current organization context.
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: Rejection payload containing the mandatory reason for returning the timesheet to draft.

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.

Create comprehensive E2E test suites for the ERP — HRM & Time Tracking Platform based on the full requirements below. Focus on realistic user flows, permission boundaries, organization scoping, validation rules, and state transitions across all API interfaces.

# ERP — HRM & Time Tracking Platform

I want to create an ERP platform focused on human resource management and time tracking.

## Organization (Multi-Tenancy)

- The platform supports multiple organizations (multi-tenancy)
- Each organization operates independently with its own employees, projects, and data
- Users create an organization during initial sign-up
- Each organization has: name, description, logo image, currency (e.g., USD, EUR, KRW), timezone, and fiscal start month
- Organization owners can edit organization settings
- Organization owners can delete their organization only if:
  - All pending timesheets are resolved (approved or rejected)
  - There are no active employee contracts
- When an organization is deleted:
  - All employees, projects, tasks, timelogs, and timesheets are permanently deleted
  - The owner's account remains but is no longer associated with any organization

## User Account

- Users sign up with email and password
- Users log in with email and password
- Users can change their password
- A user can belong to multiple organizations
- When logging in, users select which organization to work in (organization context)
- All subsequent actions are scoped to the selected organization
- Users can switch organizations without logging out
- Users can delete their account:
  - If they are the sole owner of an organization, they must transfer ownership or delete the organization first
  - Their employee records in other organizations are marked as "deactivated"

## User Profile

- Each user has a global profile with: display name, avatar image, phone number
- Users can edit their profile
- Profile is shared across all organizations the user belongs to

## Roles and Permissions

- Each organization has its own set of roles
- Three built-in roles (cannot be deleted):
  - **Owner**: full access to all features, can manage roles and members
  - **Manager**: can manage employees, projects, approve timesheets, view reports
  - **Employee**: can track time, submit timesheets, view own data
- Organization owners can create custom roles
- Each custom role has: name and a set of permissions
- Available permissions:
  - `org:manage` — edit organization settings
  - `employee:manage` — add, edit, deactivate employees
  - `employee:view` — view employee list and details
  - `project:manage` — create, edit, delete projects and tasks
  - `project:view` — view projects and tasks
  - `time:manage` — edit or delete any employee's timelogs
  - `time:approve` — approve or reject timesheets
  - `time:view_all` — view all employees' timelogs and timesheets
  - `report:view` — view organization reports
- Organization owners can edit custom roles
- Organization owners can delete custom roles only if no employees are assigned to them
- Each employee in an organization is assigned exactly one role
- Role assignment can be changed by users with `employee:manage` permission

## Employee Management

- Users with `employee:manage` permission can invite new employees to the organization
- Invitation is done by email
- If the invited email already has an account, the user is added to the organization
- If the invited email has no account, a pending invitation is created
  - When the user signs up with that email, they are automatically added to the pending organizations
- Each employee record has:
  - Reference to the user account
  - Role in this organization
  - Department (optional)
  - Position/title (optional)
  - Employment type: full-time, part-time, contractor, intern
  - Status: active, deactivated
- Users with `employee:manage` permission can edit employee records (department, position, employment type)
- Users with `employee:manage` permission can deactivate employees
  - Deactivated employees cannot log time or submit timesheets
  - Deactivated employees' historical data (timelogs, timesheets) is preserved
  - Deactivated employees can be reactivated
- Users with `employee:view` permission can view the employee list
- The employee list is paginated
- Employees can filter the list by: department, employment type, status
- Employees can search by name

## Employee Contracts

- Each employee can have multiple contracts (historical record)
- Only one contract can be active at a time
- Each contract has:
  - Start date (required)
  - End date (optional, null means ongoing)
  - Pay rate (required, numeric value)
  - Pay period: hourly, daily, weekly, monthly
  - Working hours per week (required, e.g., 40)
  - Notes (optional)
- Users with `employee:manage` permission can create contracts for employees
- Creating a new contract automatically ends the previous active contract (sets end date to the day before the new contract starts)
- Users with `employee:manage` permission can edit the current active contract
- Past contracts cannot be edited (immutable historical record)
- Employees can view their own contracts
- Users with `employee:view` permission can view any employee's contracts

## Departments

- Each organization can have departments
- Each department has: name, description, and optional parent department (one level of nesting)
- Users with `org:manage` permission can create, edit, and delete departments
- Deleting a department sets employees' department to null (does not delete employees)
- Employees can view the list of departments

## Projects

- Users with `project:manage` permission can create projects
- Each project has:
  - Name (required)
  - Description (optional)
  - Color code (for UI display, required)
  - Status: active, archived, completed
  - Budget hours (optional, total estimated hours)
  - Start date (optional)
  - End date (optional)
- Users with `project:manage` permission can edit projects
- Users with `project:manage` permission can archive or complete projects
  - Archived/completed projects cannot receive new timelogs
  - Existing timelogs on archived/completed projects are preserved
- Users with `project:manage` permission can delete projects only if:
  - The project has no timelogs associated with it
- Users with `project:view` permission can view all projects
- The project list is paginated
- Projects can be filtered by status

## Project Members

- Users with `project:manage` permission can assign employees to projects
- An employee can be assigned to multiple projects
- Each project membership has: employee, project, and assigned role (member or project-lead)
- Project leads can manage tasks within their project
- Users with `project:manage` permission can remove employees from projects
- Employees can view which projects they are assigned to

## Tasks

- Project leads or users with `project:manage` permission can create tasks within a project
- Each task has:
  - Title (required)
  - Description (optional)
  - Status: open, in-progress, completed, closed
  - Priority: low, medium, high, urgent
  - Estimated hours (optional)
  - Due date (optional)
  - Assigned employee (optional, must be a project member)
  - Parent task (optional, for subtasks — one level of nesting only)
- Project leads can edit tasks in their project
- Users with `project:manage` permission can edit any task
- Task status changes are recorded in task history
- Each task history entry records: timestamp, old status, new status, who made the change
- Employees can view tasks in projects they are assigned to
- Tasks can be filtered by: status, priority, assigned employee
- Tasks can be sorted by: due date, priority, creation date

## Time Tracking — Timelogs

- Employees can log time entries (timelogs)
- Each timelog has:
  - Date (required)
  - Duration in minutes (required)
  - Project (required, must be a project the employee is assigned to)
  - Task (optional, must belong to the selected project)
  - Description (optional, what was done)
  - Billable flag (boolean, default true)
- Employees can only create timelogs for themselves
- Employees can edit their own timelogs only if:
  - The timelog is not part of an approved timesheet
- Employees can delete their own timelogs only if:
  - The timelog is not part of any submitted or approved timesheet
- Users with `time:manage` permission can edit or delete any employee's timelogs
- Users with `time:view_all` permission can view all employees' timelogs
- Employees can view their own timelogs
- Timelogs are paginated
- Timelogs can be filtered by: date range, project, task, billable status

## Time Tracking — Timesheets

- A timesheet is a collection of timelogs for a specific week (Monday to Sunday)
- Employees submit timesheets for approval
- Each timesheet has:
  - Employee (owner)
  - Week start date (Monday)
  - Week end date (Sunday)
  - Status: draft, submitted, approved, rejected
  - Total hours (calculated from included timelogs)
  - Submitted at (timestamp)
  - Reviewed at (timestamp, when approved/rejected)
  - Reviewed by (the user who approved/rejected)
  - Rejection reason (text, required when rejecting)
- Employees can create a draft timesheet for a specific week
- Creating a draft automatically includes all timelogs for that employee in that week
- Employees can add or remove timelogs from a draft timesheet
- Employees can submit a draft timesheet for approval
  - A timesheet cannot be submitted if it has no timelogs
  - A timesheet cannot be submitted if another timesheet for the same week is already submitted or approved
- Users with `time:approve` permission can view all submitted timesheets
- Users with `time:approve` permission can approve submitted timesheets
  - Approved timesheets lock all included timelogs (cannot be edited or deleted)
- Users with `time:approve` permission can reject submitted timesheets with a reason
  - Rejected timesheets return to draft status
  - The employee can modify and resubmit the rejected timesheet
- Employees can view their own timesheets
- Timesheets are paginated
- Timesheets can be filtered by: status, date range

## Timer (Live Time Tracking)

- Employees can start a timer to track time in real-time
- Each employee can have at most one active timer at a time
- Starting a timer requires selecting a project (task is optional)
- The timer records: start timestamp, project, task, description
- Employees can stop their timer
  - Stopping the timer creates a timelog with the calculated duration
  - Duration is rounded to the nearest minute
- Employees can discard their timer (no timelog is created)
- Employees can view their currently running timer
- If an employee forgets to stop their timer, it continues running indefinitely (no automatic stop)
- Employees can edit the description and project/task of a running timer

## Reports

- Users with `report:view` permission can access organization reports
- Available reports:

**Time Report**
- Shows total hours logged per employee for a given date range
- Can be grouped by: employee, project, task
- Can be filtered by: date range, employee, project, billable status
- Shows breakdown: total hours, billable hours, non-billable hours

**Project Budget Report**
- Shows each project's budget hours vs. actual hours logged
- Shows percentage of budget consumed
- Projects without budget hours are excluded

**Weekly Summary Report**
- Shows a week-by-week summary for a given date range
- Each week shows: total hours, number of timelogs, number of employees who logged time
- Can be filtered by project

## Activity Log

- The system records significant actions as activity log entries
- Each activity log entry has: timestamp, user who performed the action, action type, target entity, and details
- Logged actions include:
  - Employee invited, deactivated, reactivated
  - Contract created or edited
  - Project created, archived, completed, deleted
  - Task status changed
  - Timesheet submitted, approved, rejected
  - Role assigned or changed
- Users with `org:manage` permission can view the full activity log
- The activity log is paginated
- The activity log can be filtered by: action type, user, date range

## Dashboard

- Each employee has a personal dashboard showing:
  - Hours logged today
  - Hours logged this week
  - Active timer status (if running)
  - Recent timelogs (last 5)
  - Pending timesheet status for current week
  - Tasks assigned to them with status "in-progress" or "open"

- Users with `report:view` permission see an organization dashboard showing:
  - Total employees (active)
  - Total hours logged this week (all employees)
  - Number of pending timesheets awaiting approval
  - Projects with budget utilization over 80%
  - Top 5 employees by hours logged this week

## Data Isolation

- All data is strictly isolated per organization
- Employees in one organization cannot see data from another organization
- Users who belong to multiple organizations only see data for their currently selected organization
- API endpoints enforce organization context on every request

scenario.draft: Test that a member with report viewing access can retrieve the organization dashboard summary for the currently selected organization using the default or specified date range. Verify the response is paginated, contains only data for the active organization, and returns the expected dashboard metrics such as active employee count, pending timesheet count, weekly hours total, and budget-utilization figures. Confirm that the response shape matches the paginated summary DTO and that the organization reference in each row belongs to the selected organization. Also verify that the endpoint does not mix in data from other organizations when the authenticated user belongs to more than one organization.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a member who has report viewing permission in the selected organization so the report endpoint can be accessed legitimately.

functions.name: test_api_organization_dashboard_summary_access

scenario.draft: Test that dashboard summary results remain strictly scoped to the active organization even when the authenticated member belongs to multiple organizations. Prepare a user context that can switch between organizations, select one organization, and request the dashboard summary with a date range that would otherwise produce data in another organization. Verify the returned summary only reflects the selected organization’s employees, timelogs, timesheets, and projects, and that metrics such as active employee count and weekly hours total do not leak cross-organization values. Also verify that switching organization context changes the dataset returned by the same endpoint as expected.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a member who can belong to multiple organizations and access reports in at least one of them.

functions.name: test_api_organization_dashboard_summary_organization_isolation

scenario.draft: Test the endpoint behavior when the requested reporting window has no matching dashboard records. Request a date range that falls outside available organization activity or otherwise resolves to an empty result set. Verify the API returns an empty paginated response rather than expanding the scope or returning records from unrelated periods. Confirm pagination metadata is still well-formed with zero records and zero pages where applicable, and that no dashboard metrics are fabricated for the empty period.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a member with report viewing permission so the empty-result behavior is tested on an authorized request path.

functions.name: test_api_organization_dashboard_summary_empty_result_range

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated member with report-view access can retrieve an organization dashboard summary snapshot that belongs to the currently selected organization. The test should create or identify a valid dashboard summary ID for the active organization, then confirm the response returns the expected snapshot fields: organization reference, snapshot date, active employee count, pending timesheet count, weekly hours total, budget-utilization-over-80 count, and optional featured-project cache values when present. Also confirm the summary is read-only and reflects precomputed data rather than recalculating live aggregates. Validate that the returned organization context matches the selected organization and that the payload preserves nullable featured-project fields when no featured project is cached.

dependencies.purpose: Create an authenticated member session because this endpoint requires member access.

functions.name: test_api_organization_dashboard_summary_view

scenario.draft: Verify organization-scoped access control for dashboard summaries by preparing the same authenticated member with access to two organizations, selecting the first organization as the active context, and obtaining or creating a dashboard summary in the second organization. Then request the second organization's dashboard summary ID while the caller remains scoped to the first organization. Confirm the API does not return a summary from another tenant and does not leak cached metrics across organization boundaries. Also verify the same endpoint behavior for a summary ID that is valid in another organization but not in the currently selected organization context.

dependencies.purpose: Create an authenticated member session because access control is evaluated in the member context.

functions.name: test_api_organization_dashboard_summary_cross_organization_access

scenario.draft: Verify the endpoint's behavior for dashboard snapshots that exist but are no longer active because they have been soft-deleted or otherwise invalidated. The test should use a summary ID whose deletedAt is set, or otherwise represent an invalidated snapshot row for the selected organization, and confirm the service does not return stale dashboard data when the business rules treat inactive snapshots as unavailable. The response should align with the platform's not-found or access-control policy for inactive snapshots, ensuring the organization dashboard only exposes active cached summaries.

dependencies.purpose: Create an authenticated member session because the endpoint is member-scoped.

functions.name: test_api_organization_dashboard_summary_inactive_snapshot_rejected

scenario.draft: Test the authenticated member’s personal dashboard summary in the currently selected organization. Verify the response returns the current employee’s precomputed snapshot with the organization-scoped metrics needed for rendering the dashboard: hours logged today, hours logged this week, active timer state and start timestamp, recent timelog count, pending timesheet status for the current week, and open/in-progress assigned task counts. Confirm the response is limited to the selected organization and does not expose another employee’s summary data. Also verify that pagination controls in the request are honored in the response envelope, while the payload remains a dashboard summary page for the current member. Cover the case where the dashboard snapshot already exists and is returned with its stored timestamps and counts unchanged, and the case where the snapshot has been logically invalidated or rebuilt from underlying data but still resolves to the latest derived state for the current employee. Include a negative business-rule check that a member without a valid selected organization context, or whose membership is inactive, cannot obtain the dashboard summary for that organization scope.

dependencies.purpose: Create an authenticated member session so the dashboard endpoint can resolve the current employee context.

functions.name: test_api_employee_dashboard_summary_current_member

scenario.draft: Test that the dashboard summary reflects live work-state changes for the authenticated member in the selected organization. After establishing member access, prepare a context where the employee has an active timer, recently logged timelogs, and assigned tasks in open and in-progress states, then call the dashboard summary endpoint and verify the returned snapshot surfaces the active timer flag and start time, recent timelog count, today/week hour totals, and the assigned task counts consistently. Then validate the same endpoint when the employee has no active timer and no pending timesheet for the current week: the response should keep the active timer fields null/false as appropriate and return the current pending timesheet status without fabricating values. This scenario focuses on the business projection behavior of the dashboard summary rather than source-record retrieval, ensuring the endpoint is suitable for UI rendering from a single call.

dependencies.purpose: Create an authenticated member session so the dashboard endpoint can resolve the current employee context.

functions.name: test_api_employee_dashboard_summary_live_work_state

scenario.draft: Test organization isolation for the employee dashboard summary. Establish a member account and ensure the user belongs to more than one organization context, then request the dashboard summary while the selected organization is set to one organization and verify only that organization’s employee dashboard snapshot is returned. Repeat the same endpoint call after switching the selected organization context and confirm the summary changes to the other organization’s employee data rather than reusing the previous organization’s metrics. Include a business-rule check that the endpoint never exposes counts, task status, timers, or timelog data from a different organization even when the same member has access elsewhere. This scenario validates that the dashboard is strictly scoped to the active organization and the current employee in that organization.

dependencies.purpose: Create an authenticated member session so the dashboard endpoint can resolve the current employee context.

functions.name: test_api_employee_dashboard_summary_organization_isolation

scenario.draft:
Verify that an authenticated member can retrieve the current employee dashboard summary only in the currently selected organization context. The main success path should confirm the response returns the personal dashboard snapshot for the caller’s employee record, including today’s hours, week-to-date hours, active timer state, recent timelog count, pending timesheet status, and assigned task counts. Validate that the payload is scoped to the selected organization and reflects the caller’s accessible employee data rather than another member’s data.

Also cover the case where the member belongs to more than one organization: after switching organization context, the endpoint should return the summary for the newly selected organization, with values appropriate to that context. Ensure the test confirms the response is a precomputed snapshot and not a partially assembled result.

Include the important negative behavior that if the member has no selected organization or no accessible employee snapshot exists for the selected organization, the endpoint should fail with a not-found or access-style error instead of returning partial dashboard data.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate a member account so the dashboard endpoint can be accessed with a valid member token.
Create or prepare the organization context and membership needed to ensure the dashboard is resolved within the selected organization.

functions.name: test_api_employee_dashboard_summary_selected_organization

scenario.draft:
Verify that the dashboard summary is denied when the caller does not have an active selected organization context or cannot resolve an accessible employee record in that organization. The test should attempt to call the endpoint after member authentication but before selecting a usable organization context, and assert the API rejects the request rather than constructing a synthetic dashboard snapshot.

Cover the situation where the member account exists but is not associated with the target organization, or the employee context is unavailable because the membership is inactive. The endpoint should return a clear access-related or not-found style failure and must not expose any cross-organization dashboard information. This scenario is important because the dashboard is explicitly scoped to the current organization and should never leak summary data from another tenant.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate a member account so the failure can be evaluated against a valid signed-in user session.

functions.name: test_api_employee_dashboard_summary_missing_organization_context

scenario.draft:
Verify that the dashboard summary remains organization-isolated when the same member belongs to multiple organizations. Prepare two organization contexts for the same authenticated user, then confirm the endpoint returns only the snapshot for the organization currently selected in the session. The response should reflect that organization’s employee relation, hours logged, active timer state, pending timesheet status, and assigned task counters, with no data from the other organization leaking into the payload.

This scenario should also confirm that switching the selected organization changes the returned summary accordingly. The test is successful only if each call returns the correct organization-specific snapshot and the response remains bounded to the active context. If one organization has no dashboard snapshot available, the API should return a not-found style error for that context rather than falling back to the other organization’s data.

scenario.draft: Verify that a member with organization management access can browse the activity log for the currently selected organization and receive a paginated, newest-first list of summary entries. The test should set up a member in an organization where supported significant actions already exist in the activity log, then request the first page with a reasonable limit and confirm the response contains only entries from that organization. Validate that each returned item exposes the actor, action type, target entity reference, details, and timestamps, and that the page metadata is consistent with the returned slice. Also confirm that the endpoint is read-only by ensuring it only returns summary data and does not expose mutable fields or cross-organization records.

functions.name: test_api_activity_log_entries_browse_organization_history

scenario.draft: Verify browsing and filtering behavior for the organization activity log by action type and acting member, including the empty-result case. Prepare the selected organization with multiple activity entries covering at least two supported action types and multiple actors, then request the list with a specific action type filter and separately with a specific acting-member filter. Confirm that each filtered response returns only matching entries, preserves pagination metadata, and returns an empty page when no records match the filter. Validate that the response remains scoped to the currently selected organization and does not include activity entries from other organizations.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a member before browsing organization activity log entries.

functions.name: test_api_activity_log_entries_filter_by_action_and_member

scenario.draft: Verify access control and supported search constraints for the activity log endpoint. First, confirm that an authenticated member without the organization management permission cannot browse the activity log and is denied access. Then confirm that a member with the required permission can query the endpoint using a bounded date range and receive only entries whose timestamps fall within that range. Also validate that the endpoint rejects unsupported browsing behavior at the business level, such as returning records outside the selected organization or including unsupported activity types, while still keeping the operation read-only.

dependencies.purpose: Create an authenticated member session for the negative and positive access checks.

functions.name: test_api_activity_log_entries_permission_and_date_scope

scenario.draft: Verify that a member with organization management permission can retrieve a single activity log entry that belongs to the currently selected organization. The test should create or use an activity log entry generated by a significant organization action in the active organization, then request it by ID and assert the response returns the full read-only audit record with the correct activity log ID, organization reference, performing member reference, action type, target entity type and ID, details, timestamps, and nullable deletedAt value. Also confirm the response does not mutate the record and that the returned organization/member references are lightweight summary objects rather than expanded mutable entities. This scenario should cover the primary successful lookup path and validate organization scoping within the selected tenant.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a member who has organization management permission in the target organization, since this endpoint is restricted to that role and the active organization context determines visibility.

functions.name: test_api_activity_log_entry_retrieve_by_organization_manager

scenario.draft: Verify organization isolation for activity log retrieval by attempting to read an entry that exists in a different organization than the currently selected one. The setup should authenticate a member, ensure the member is operating in one organization, and prepare an activity log entry in another organization. When the request is sent using the foreign entry ID, the API should not reveal cross-tenant data and should respond with a not-found style result rather than returning another organization's audit record. This scenario validates that the endpoint enforces tenant scoping before lookup results are exposed.

scenario.draft: Verify that a member without organization management permission cannot access the detailed activity log entry even when the entry belongs to the currently selected organization. The test should use a member account in the organization context that has a non-management role, attempt to retrieve an existing activity log entry by ID, and assert that access is denied with a forbidden-style response rather than leaking the audit details. This scenario is important because activity logs contain sensitive history and are only intended for organization managers.

Verify the request succeeds when the target owner already belongs to the selected organization, the response returns the organization with the owner updated, and the organization itself remains intact. Also cover a business-rule failure case where the authenticated member is not allowed to transfer ownership or the target member is not part of the organization, and confirm the API rejects the transfer without changing the current owner.

This scenario should also confirm that the operation does not delete or recreate the organization, only updates the ownership reference when all rules are satisfied.

Verify the response represents the invited email, indicates a pending workflow state, and does not attach a member summary yet. Also verify that sending the same invitation again for the same organization-email pair does not create a duplicate pending invitation and returns the existing workflow result or an equivalent non-duplicating outcome. Ensure the test uses one organization context only and does not affect any other organization memberships for the same email.

functions.name: test_api_employee_invitation_pending_email

Verify that the request attaches that existing account to the current organization instead of creating a pending invitation, and that the response includes the invited email and linked member summary. Confirm the behavior is scoped to the currently selected organization and does not affect the user’s memberships in any other organizations. Also verify the repeated invitation flow for the same email remains organization-scoped and does not create an additional pending invitation in the current organization when the account is already linked.

functions.name: test_api_employee_invitation_existing_account_attachment

scenario.draft: Test that the invitation endpoint enforces organization-scoped authorization and invitation uniqueness rules. First verify a member without employee-management permission cannot create an invitation in the selected organization. Then verify that a valid invitation request using an email that is already associated with the organization or otherwise cannot be matched to a new invite is rejected according to the business rule, rather than creating duplicate membership or invitation records. This scenario should focus on permission boundary and duplicate-prevention behavior, not payload-format validation.

Seed multiple invitation records in the selected organization, including at least one pending invitation and one invitation that has already connected to an account, and confirm the response returns only organization-scoped records, exposes lightweight summary fields only, and includes the related member summary when the invitation is linked to an existing account. Validate search/filter behavior by email, status, and free-text query, and confirm that results remain constrained to the currently selected organization even when the same email or invitation state exists in another organization. Also verify that the endpoint reflects deduplication/stable summary behavior when repeated invitation events exist for the same target email within the organization.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a member who has employee management permission in the selected organization before browsing invitations.

functions.name: test_api_employee_invitations_list_by_organization

Set up a logged-in member whose organization role lacks employee management rights, then call the invitations list endpoint and confirm access is rejected rather than exposing any invitation data. This scenario should focus on the authorization boundary for the list operation and ensure the rule is enforced before any organization-scoped invitation browsing occurs.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a member without employee management permission in the selected organization so the access-control boundary can be exercised.

functions.name: test_api_employee_invitations_requires_employee_management_permission

scenario.draft: Verify that the invitation list honors pagination controls and returns consistent page metadata for different pages of the same organization-scoped dataset. Create enough invitation records to span multiple pages, request the first page and a later page using the browse criteria, and confirm that pagination metadata reports the correct current page, page size, total records, and total page count. Also validate that each page contains only the subset of invitations for that page, with no duplication across pages and no leakage from other organizations’ invitation records.

scenario.draft: Test deactivating an active employee in the current organization by a member with employee management permission. Verify the response returns the updated employee record with status changed to deactivated, while the employee still exists in the organization and retains historical data references such as timelogs, timesheets, and contracts. Confirm that the deactivation is recorded as an activity log entry with the correct actor, target employee, action type, and change details. Confirm the employee remains deactivated, historical records are preserved, and no additional deactivation activity log entry is created for the repeated request.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a member who can manage employees so the deactivation attempt is evaluated under valid permissions.

functions.name: test_api_employee_deactivate_other_organization_employee

Confirm that historical data is not altered by the operation by checking that the employee's existing timelogs, timesheets, and contract history remain intact after reactivation. Also verify that the system records the employee reactivation activity log entry for the acting member and the target employee as part of the same business workflow.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a member with the permissions needed to reactivate employees.

functions.name: test_api_employee_reactivate_deactivated_employee

scenario.draft: Verify that a deactivated employee in the currently selected organization can be reactivated successfully by an authenticated member, and that the employee returns to active status without affecting other organizations. Prepare the authenticated member context first, then ensure the target employee is deactivated in the same organization, perform reactivation, and confirm the employee status changes to active and no duplicate reactivation occurs. Also confirm that the operation does not apply to employees outside the selected organization context by using a separate organization-scoped fixture, but keep the primary focus on a valid reactivation workflow rather than validation-style rejection cases.

Finally, cover the access-control and isolation behaviors by confirming that unauthorized access to another employee’s contract history is denied and that requesting an employee outside the current organization does not reveal cross-organization data.

Also verify the same denial behavior when the caller remains in the correct tenant but lacks permission to view that employee's contract history. The scenario should focus on organization isolation and authorization enforcement, not on contract content or input validation.

Validate that the endpoint reflects the stable historical record, including unchanged pay rate, pay period, working hours, notes, and dates for past contracts. The test should also assert that the endpoint does not attempt any derived updates or backfill behavior: it must simply read and return the ordered history. If the employee has only one ongoing contract, confirm the endpoint still returns a valid history with a null end date and no duplicate records.

The scenario should also confirm the check is scoped to the selected organization and that it does not leak information about roles from other organizations.

instruction:
Implement the API functions for the ERP — HRM & Time Tracking Platform based on the full requirements below. Generate the business logic/service provider code that matches the already-defined API interfaces, including validation, authorization, organization scoping, state transitions, and data consistency rules.

# ERP — HRM & Time Tracking Platform

I want to create an ERP platform focused on human resource management and time tracking.

## Organization (Multi-Tenancy)

- The platform supports multiple organizations (multi-tenancy)
- Each organization operates independently with its own employees, projects, and data
- Users create an organization during initial sign-up
- Each organization has: name, description, logo image, currency (e.g., USD, EUR, KRW), timezone, and fiscal start month
- Organization owners can edit organization settings
- Organization owners can delete their organization only if:
  - All pending timesheets are resolved (approved or rejected)
  - There are no active employee contracts
- When an organization is deleted:
  - All employees, projects, tasks, timelogs, and timesheets are permanently deleted
  - The owner's account remains but is no longer associated with any organization

## User Account

- Users sign up with email and password
- Users log in with email and password
- Users can change their password
- A user can belong to multiple organizations
- When logging in, users select which organization to work in (organization context)
- All subsequent actions are scoped to the selected organization
- Users can switch organizations without logging out
- Users can delete their account:
  - If they are the sole owner of an organization, they must transfer ownership or delete the organization first
  - Their employee records in other organizations are marked as "deactivated"

## User Profile

- Each user has a global profile with: display name, avatar image, phone number
- Users can edit their profile
- Profile is shared across all organizations the user belongs to

## Roles and Permissions

- Each organization has its own set of roles
- Three built-in roles (cannot be deleted):
  - **Owner**: full access to all features, can manage roles and members
  - **Manager**: can manage employees, projects, approve timesheets, view reports
  - **Employee**: can track time, submit timesheets, view own data
- Organization owners can create custom roles
- Each custom role has: name and a set of permissions
- Available permissions:
  - `org:manage` — edit organization settings
  - `employee:manage` — add, edit, deactivate employees
  - `employee:view` — view employee list and details
  - `project:manage` — create, edit, delete projects and tasks
  - `project:view` — view projects and tasks
  - `time:manage` — edit or delete any employee's timelogs
  - `time:approve` — approve or reject timesheets
  - `time:view_all` — view all employees' timelogs and timesheets
  - `report:view` — view organization reports
- Organization owners can edit custom roles
- Organization owners can delete custom roles only if no employees are assigned to them
- Each employee in an organization is assigned exactly one role
- Role assignment can be changed by users with `employee:manage` permission

## Employee Management

- Users with `employee:manage` permission can invite new employees to the organization
- Invitation is done by email
- If the invited email already has an account, the user is added to the organization
- If the invited email has no account, a pending invitation is created
  - When the user signs up with that email, they are automatically added to the pending organizations
- Each employee record has:
  - Reference to the user account
  - Role in this organization
  - Department (optional)
  - Position/title (optional)
  - Employment type: full-time, part-time, contractor, intern
  - Status: active, deactivated
- Users with `employee:manage` permission can edit employee records (department, position, employment type)
- Users with `employee:manage` permission can deactivate employees
  - Deactivated employees cannot log time or submit timesheets
  - Deactivated employees' historical data (timelogs, timesheets) is preserved
  - Deactivated employees can be reactivated
- Users with `employee:view` permission can view the employee list
- The employee list is paginated
- Employees can filter the list by: department, employment type, status
- Employees can search by name

## Employee Contracts

- Each employee can have multiple contracts (historical record)
- Only one contract can be active at a time
- Each contract has:
  - Start date (required)
  - End date (optional, null means ongoing)
  - Pay rate (required, numeric value)
  - Pay period: hourly, daily, weekly, monthly
  - Working hours per week (required, e.g., 40)
  - Notes (optional)
- Users with `employee:manage` permission can create contracts for employees
- Creating a new contract automatically ends the previous active contract (sets end date to the day before the new contract starts)
- Users with `employee:manage` permission can edit the current active contract
- Past contracts cannot be edited (immutable historical record)
- Employees can view their own contracts
- Users with `employee:view` permission can view any employee's contracts

## Departments

- Each organization can have departments
- Each department has: name, description, and optional parent department (one level of nesting)
- Users with `org:manage` permission can create, edit, and delete departments
- Deleting a department sets employees' department to null (does not delete employees)
- Employees can view the list of departments

## Projects

- Users with `project:manage` permission can create projects
- Each project has:
  - Name (required)
  - Description (optional)
  - Color code (for UI display, required)
  - Status: active, archived, completed
  - Budget hours (optional, total estimated hours)
  - Start date (optional)
  - End date (optional)
- Users with `project:manage` permission can edit projects
- Users with `project:manage` permission can archive or complete projects
  - Archived/completed projects cannot receive new timelogs
  - Existing timelogs on archived/completed projects are preserved
- Users with `project:manage` permission can delete projects only if:
  - The project has no timelogs associated with it
- Users with `project:view` permission can view all projects
- The project list is paginated
- Projects can be filtered by status

## Project Members

- Users with `project:manage` permission can assign employees to projects
- An employee can be assigned to multiple projects
- Each project membership has: employee, project, and assigned role (member or project-lead)
- Project leads can manage tasks within their project
- Users with `project:manage` permission can remove employees from projects
- Employees can view which projects they are assigned to

## Tasks

- Project leads or users with `project:manage` permission can create tasks within a project
- Each task has:
  - Title (required)
  - Description (optional)
  - Status: open, in-progress, completed, closed
  - Priority: low, medium, high, urgent
  - Estimated hours (optional)
  - Due date (optional)
  - Assigned employee (optional, must be a project member)
  - Parent task (optional, for subtasks — one level of nesting only)
- Project leads can edit tasks in their project
- Users with `project:manage` permission can edit any task
- Task status changes are recorded in task history
- Each task history entry records: timestamp, old status, new status, who made the change
- Employees can view tasks in projects they are assigned to
- Tasks can be filtered by: status, priority, assigned employee
- Tasks can be sorted by: due date, priority, creation date

## Time Tracking — Timelogs

- Employees can log time entries (timelogs)
- Each timelog has:
  - Date (required)
  - Duration in minutes (required)
  - Project (required, must be a project the employee is assigned to)
  - Task (optional, must belong to the selected project)
  - Description (optional, what was done)
  - Billable flag (boolean, default true)
- Employees can only create timelogs for themselves
- Employees can edit their own timelogs only if:
  - The timelog is not part of an approved timesheet
- Employees can delete their own timelogs only if:
  - The timelog is not part of any submitted or approved timesheet
- Users with `time:manage` permission can edit or delete any employee's timelogs
- Users with `time:view_all` permission can view all employees' timelogs
- Employees can view their own timelogs
- Timelogs are paginated
- Timelogs can be filtered by: date range, project, task, billable status

## Time Tracking — Timesheets

- A timesheet is a collection of timelogs for a specific week (Monday to Sunday)
- Employees submit timesheets for approval
- Each timesheet has:
  - Employee (owner)
  - Week start date (Monday)
  - Week end date (Sunday)
  - Status: draft, submitted, approved, rejected
  - Total hours (calculated from included timelogs)
  - Submitted at (timestamp)
  - Reviewed at (timestamp, when approved/rejected)
  - Reviewed by (the user who approved/rejected)
  - Rejection reason (text, required when rejecting)
- Employees can create a draft timesheet for a specific week
- Creating a draft automatically includes all timelogs for that employee in that week
- Employees can add or remove timelogs from a draft timesheet
- Employees can submit a draft timesheet for approval
  - A timesheet cannot be submitted if it has no timelogs
  - A timesheet cannot be submitted if another timesheet for the same week is already submitted or approved
- Users with `time:approve` permission can view all submitted timesheets
- Users with `time:approve` permission can approve submitted timesheets
  - Approved timesheets lock all included timelogs (cannot be edited or deleted)
- Users with `time:approve` permission can reject submitted timesheets with a reason
  - Rejected timesheets return to draft status
  - The employee can modify and resubmit the rejected timesheet
- Employees can view their own timesheets
- Timesheets are paginated
- Timesheets can be filtered by: status, date range

## Timer (Live Time Tracking)

- Employees can start a timer to track time in real-time
- Each employee can have at most one active timer at a time
- Starting a timer requires selecting a project (task is optional)
- The timer records: start timestamp, project, task, description
- Employees can stop their timer
  - Stopping the timer creates a timelog with the calculated duration
  - Duration is rounded to the nearest minute
- Employees can discard their timer (no timelog is created)
- Employees can view their currently running timer
- If an employee forgets to stop their timer, it continues running indefinitely (no automatic stop)
- Employees can edit the description and project/task of a running timer

## Reports

- Users with `report:view` permission can access organization reports
- Available reports:

**Time Report**
- Shows total hours logged per employee for a given date range
- Can be grouped by: employee, project, task
- Can be filtered by: date range, employee, project, billable status
- Shows breakdown: total hours, billable hours, non-billable hours

**Project Budget Report**
- Shows each project's budget hours vs. actual hours logged
- Shows percentage of budget consumed
- Projects without budget hours are excluded

**Weekly Summary Report**
- Shows a week-by-week summary for a given date range
- Each week shows: total hours, number of timelogs, number of employees who logged time
- Can be filtered by project

## Activity Log

- The system records significant actions as activity log entries
- Each activity log entry has: timestamp, user who performed the action, action type, target entity, and details
- Logged actions include:
  - Employee invited, deactivated, reactivated
  - Contract created or edited
  - Project created, archived, completed, deleted
  - Task status changed
  - Timesheet submitted, approved, rejected
  - Role assigned or changed
- Users with `org:manage` permission can view the full activity log
- The activity log is paginated
- The activity log can be filtered by: action type, user, date range

## Dashboard

- Each employee has a personal dashboard showing:
  - Hours logged today
  - Hours logged this week
  - Active timer status (if running)
  - Recent timelogs (last 5)
  - Pending timesheet status for current week
  - Tasks assigned to them with status "in-progress" or "open"

- Users with `report:view` permission see an organization dashboard showing:
  - Total employees (active)
  - Total hours logged this week (all employees)
  - Number of pending timesheets awaiting approval
  - Projects with budget utilization over 80%
  - Top 5 employees by hours logged this week

## Data Isolation

- All data is strictly isolated per organization
- Employees in one organization cannot see data from another organization
- Users who belong to multiple organizations only see data for their currently selected organization
- API endpoints enforce organization context on every request
